ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Question: Consider a silicon sample at \( T = 300 \, K \), with a uniform donor density \( N_d = 5 \times 10^{16} \, \text{cm}^{-3} \) illuminated uniformly such that the optical generation rate is \( G_{\text{opt}} = 1.5 \times 10^{20} \, \text{cm}^{-3} \text{s}^{-1} \) throughout the sample. The incident radiation is turned off at \( t = 0 \). Assume low-level injection to be valid and ignore surface effects. The carrier lifetimes are \( \tau_{p0} = 0.1 \, \mu s \) and \( \tau_{n0} = 0.5 \, \mu s \).

The hole concentration at \( t = 0 \) and the hole concentration at \( t = 0.3 \, \mu s \), respectively, are:

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Given Gopt = 1.5 × 10^20 cm^-3 s^-1 and the minority carrier hole lifetime τp0 = 0.1 μs. Convert the lifetime: 0.1 μs = 1.0 × 10^-7 s. At t = 0, immediately when the illumination is turned off, the carrier concentration is still the illuminated steady-state value. Under low-level injection, the excess hole concentration is Δp = Gopt τp0 = (1.5 × 10^20)(1.0 × 10^-7) = 1.5 × 10^13 cm^-3. The equilibrium minority hole concentration in n-type silicon is negligible compared with this excess value, so p(0) ≈ Δp.

planner_metadata.knowledge_role: In uniformly illuminated n-type silicon under low-level injection, holes are the minority excess carriers. At steady state just before shutoff, optical generation balances recombination: Gopt = Δp/τp0, so Δp = Gopt τp0. The total hole concentration is p(0)=p0+Δp, with p0=ni^2/Nd negligible compared with the excess value.

method.method_draft: Set up the uniform minority-hole rate equation before t=0: dp/dt = Gopt - (p-p0)/τp0. For the steady illuminated condition just before the light is turned off, set dp/dt=0 or take the long-time limit of the ODE solution, giving p(0^-)=p0+Goptτp0. At switching, p cannot jump instantaneously, so p(0)=p(0^-). Use τp0=0.1 μs=10^-7 s and Gopt=1.5×10^20 cm^-3 s^-1 to get Goptτp0=1.5×10^13 cm^-3; p0 from Nd at 300 K is many orders smaller, so p(0)=1.5×10^13 cm^-3.
